subject: Logic
title: Tautologies and Contradictions
description: A quick, practical guide to Tautologies and Contradictions.

hook.text: "It's either raining or not raining." True no matter what. That's a tautology—always true by structure.

buildup.text: A tautology is a formula that's true in every row of its truth table. P ∨ ¬P is the classic example.

discovery.text: A contradiction is always false. P ∧ ¬P—something is both true and false—fails in every row.

twist.text: Contingent formulas are neither: sometimes true, sometimes false depending on the variable values.

climax.text: Tautologies are logical laws. They hold regardless of facts—pure structural guarantees.
